confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from six web searches in total: one for the RBA rate and five for Tokyo prices. The price searches returned crowd-sourced indexes (Expatistan, Wise and similar aggregators) and travel guides, which are rough and vary by source and date. Restaurant meals, beer and coffee are fairly well supported: inexpensive meal about ¥1,200, mid-range meal for two about $43-45, draft beer about ¥600-800, cappuccino about ¥555-603. Cocktail and wine had thin direct data. Casual venues showed cocktails at about ¥500-700 and bars at ¥1,000-2,000, with wine at about ¥1,000 or more per glass. I set both from that range and their usual premium over beer, and they are the least certain food and drink anchors. I converted yen to USD at roughly ¥155-158 per USD, the rate implied by the aggregator pages, and I did not verify a current JPY rate. The RBA rate is the 18 Nov 2026 figure reported in the search result for the RBA's exchange-rate pages. I did not open the page directly, and the search summary noted some conflicting older entries that I ignored. The accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge and were not searched or checked against any listings. They are the most uncertain anchors, because Tokyo prices swing widely with season, event demand and the yen.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was used. Tokyo anchors are based directly on Tokyo price data and aggregator averages. Accommodation reflects my general sense of Tokyo hostel, business-hotel and 3-star pricing.
